identity_policy: Exact equality of canonical full isomeric SMILES of source and the already-chosen ChEMBL molecule using RDKit 2025.09.1. Preserve fragments, charge and stereochemistry; no new candidate choice, salt stripping, neutralization, stereo completion or tautomer rescue.
annotation_policy: Use every untruncated local raw mechanism record with a nonempty non-Unknown mechanism_of_action and molecule_chembl_id equal to the already-chosen molecule ID. A linked target must have its raw target payload and tax_id=9606, organism=Homo sapiens; missing target IDs are permitted for mechanism text only. Record all exclusions.
source_policy: Local ChEMBL snapshot retrieved 2026-07-16, raw source_statuses must declare ChEMBL_37. This is the embedded source statement, not independent verification of remote release or transactional consistency.
knowledge_text_policy: Mechanisms of action: followed by lexically sorted distinct original mechanism strings separated by semicolon and a final period. No synonyms, identifiers, approval/disease fields, manually supplied knowledge, target-name duplication or response-dependent choice. No truncation.
augmentation_policy: Append exactly one space and knowledge text to the frozen complete_metadata source_name prompt. knowledge_only contains the same knowledge text without appended entity, cell line, exposure or source ID.

cohorts.mechanism_text: Exact-identity source entities with at least one allowed informative mechanism record; all existing main-eligible atoms of these entities.
cohorts.human_target: Subset of mechanism_text with at least one linked human target ChEMBL ID; binary multi-hot set of IDs, no all-zero missing target vector.
cohorts.morgan: All existing 2250 primary atoms, 188 source entities; full-source Morgan prior already frozen independently. Not restricted by mechanism availability.

inference_scope: Conservative verified coverage in one study. Missing or identity-unverified annotation does not mean absence of biology. Native human target IDs include protein families, complexes and nucleic-acid targets; do not call them a gene-target network.
